context_requirements: Osteoclast lineage or osteoclast-like cells (e.g., RAW 264.7) for direct anti-resorptive activity
Osteoblast lineage (e.g., MC3T3-E1) for anabolic/osteogenic responses
Bone microenvironment signaling (RANKL, BMP-2, cathepsin K processing) not present in the nine carcinoma lines
falsifiers: Reproducible, dose-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine carcinoma lines
Enrichment of osteoclast/osteoblast differentiation or bone-remodeling gene signatures after treatment
Selective sensitivity of any line that correlates with osteoclast-lineage markers

evidence.supports: Bone resorption inhibitors act on osteoclasts (bisphosphonates induce osteoclast apoptosis; RANKL inhibitors and SERMs block osteoclast formation), i.e., their pharmacology is bone-cell specific.
Palmatine induces apoptosis in the osteoclast precursor line RAW 264.7 via iNOS/NO, demonstrating that anti-resorptive activity is restricted to osteoclast-lineage cells.
Ulmus davidiana acts as a bone-resorption inhibitor by preventing cathepsin K maturation in osteoclasts and promoting osteoblast differentiation/mineralization in MC3T3-E1 cells.
Drynariae Rhizoma inhibits bone resorption via cathepsin K processing in osteoclasts and stimulates osteoblast differentiation in MC3T3-E1 cells, confirming bone-cell-restricted mechanism.
